subject: Allowlist handoff and firewall expectations for private runtime deployment
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private runtime: allowlist & firewall details (diagram attached)

Jonas —

Thanks for the walkthrough today. Per our security checklist we need a concise list of all "egress" and "ingress" expectations for the Redwood private runtime before we open change control. Attached is our current network diagram (acme_network_diagram_v2.pdf).

Specifically can you confirm: 1) outbound IPs and ports that must be permitted from our private connector; 2) whether Redwood expects direct Internet egress or a proxy/NAT hop; 3) any TLS SNI/ALPN expectations for deep inspection devices; and 4) recommended firewall labels (FQDNs / IP blocks) we can include in our firewall rule set.

We'd like to get this into our change board by Sep 20. If you can provide a CSV we can load into our change request template that would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Lina Torres
Network Operations
Acme Health

<attachment: acme_network_diagram_v2.pdf>

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>, security@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private runtime: allowlist & firewall details (diagram attached)

Lina — thanks for the clear ask and for the diagram. Attaching a concise allowlist template (redwood_private_allowlist_template.csv) and a short summary below you can drop into change control.

Summary (minimal required rules for Redwood Private connector):
- Destination (control plane): ctl.redwood-inference.com (TLS 443) — outbound, IP ranges: 18.128.0.0/18, 34.216.0.0/15 (we provide overlapping ranges; prefer FQDN allow if your firewall supports TLS-inspected FQDN).
- Destination (model pulls / artifact distribution): model-cdn.redwood-inference.com (TLS 443) — outbound to ranges: 52.204.0.0/16, 3.101.0.0/16.
- NTP: time.redwood-inference.com (UDP 123) — outbound (optional if you have appliance time sync).
- Health & metrics push (optional): metrics-us.redwood-inference.com (TLS 443).

Ports: all outbound over 443 (primarily) — we fall back to 80 for legacy CDN redirects but recommend blocking 80 and allowing 443 only.

Proxy/NAT: Redwood supports both models. For stricter controls we recommend:
1) Egress flows NAT'd through your perimeter proxy (recommended for auditing); 
2) OR static egress IP(s) from your NAT gateway pinned in our console so we can allowlist on our side for additional verification.

TLS SNI/ALPN: We use standard TLS 1.2/1.3 with SNI; if you perform TLS interception please ensure SNI passthrough to allow FQDN-based rules. We do not require any custom ALPN beyond http/1.1 or h2.

Attachments: the CSV has two tabs — "required" and "recommended". In short, required = outbound 443 to control plane and model CDN ranges; recommended = uptime telemetry and optional artifact prefetch ranges.

Next steps: I can join your change board call if you want a 10-minute readout. Marissa — looping you in for canary timing and any commercial notes. Ben — FYI on the static-IP option; if Acme wants static egress we need to coordinate ticketing.

Best,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Lina — thanks for the quick turnaround Jonas. A couple of small commercial/ops notes from our side:
- Canary: we recommend a 48-hour canary window using your staging VPC before production cutover. During canary we will route a small percentage of requests through the private runtime and monitor latency/connection errors.
- Static egress IP option: if Acme wants static egress IPs there is an onboarding fee and a 2-week provisioning lead time (Ben, please confirm exact lead).
- Contracts: procurement, I'll upload the addendum that covers egress responsibilities to the HubSpot deal (see link below). Can you confirm if Acme requires a signed Appendix B (networking addendum)?

If the security team approves the CSV I can send a DocuSign for the Appendix and we can schedule the canary for the week of Sep 27.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Marissa —

Appreciate the detail. A couple of clarifications before we mark the change request green: 
1) The control-plane FQDNs you listed are acceptable. Can you provide a short-lived proof-of-egress test (curl to an endpoint returning a small JSON blob) we can run from our staging NAT to validate outbound connectivity? That would save a lot of triage time.
2) For static egress IPs: we will accept up to two IPv4 addresses (we will document them in the ticket). Please confirm whether Redwood will accept those IPs being present in the request headers for accountability, or if we need to coordinate an mTLS pod-to-control-plane step (prefer minimal changes).
3) Appendix B: yes, please send via DocuSign. Procurement will sign pending the canary results.

We'll proceed with the change board submission once we receive the test endpoint and the DocuSign link.

—Acme Security
